column3: Inverts the focus's guidance-to-a-path pattern by directing false worship toward the path of Hell.
Directly pairs divine guidance with placement upon a straight path.
Its prohibition on exchanging the vile for the good supplies a concrete moral contrast for tayyib speech.
Joins release from darkness with a path explicitly characterized by the Praiseworthy.
Opens the immediate contrast between disputants whose destinies diverge before the focus's guided believers.
Uses tayyib for what is lawfully received, extending goodness beyond mere appearance.
Describes revealed truth as guiding to the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy One.
Connects being rightly guided with belonging to the sound path, while preserving the waiting context.
Links purity and a greeting of peace with admission to the Garden, giving tayyib an eschatological outcome.
Names God as the Praiseworthy, but adds little beyond the title already present in the focus.
Continues the nearby punishment scene, functioning only as a contrast to the focus's destination.

Adds another nearby punishment detail already adequately represented by the preceding parent-scene cards.

Presents received guidance to a straight path as a committed religious orientation.

Repeats the immediate punishment contrast without adding a new relation to the focus.

Connects gratitude and the Praiseworthy title, but only indirectly to guided speech and path.
Presents revelation as light that guides and the Messenger as directing to a straight path.
Sets apart the vile from the good, furnishing a strong purity contrast though outside speech.
Introduces the clear Book and light that the following verse makes a means of guidance.
Makes worship of the shared Lord the defining content of a straight path.
Uses good and bad land as an indirect analogy for fruitful versus unfruitful goodness.
Commands following Abraham's upright way, extending the path motif through inherited practice.
Pairs the purified with a greeting of peace and entry into the Garden.
Uses separation of vile from good to frame discernment before faithful commitment.
Shows harmful private speech aligned against revelation, a secondary contrast to good speech.

Restricts public evil speech, directly marking a negative boundary for good utterance.
Turns distress caused by speech toward praise and prostration, supporting the praise-side of the focus.
States that the defiantly corrupt are not guided, a general contrary boundary.
Sets guidance against the fulfilled word of Hell, echoing the alternative destination in the focus's nearby context.
Extends praise into continued worship, though the route relation remains indirect.
Associates unmingled faith with security and being guided, without specifying the path or speech.

Identifies hostile speech as the source of constriction that the next verses answer with praise and worship.
Requires recognized good speech within material responsibility, a secondary social instance of sound utterance.
Combines God's call to the abode of peace with guidance to a straight path.
Its reward-and-punishment division has no distinct speech or path contribution beyond earlier contrasts.
Treats a false doctrinal assertion as warning-worthy speech, a distant quality-of-speech contrast.
Provides the direct prayer for guidance upon the straight path.
Links obedience with preserving deeds, but does not materially clarify good speech or the praised path.

Persistent grave sin adds no distinct account of speech, praise, or guidance.

Shows that a profession of faith can be speech without inward reality.
Commands worship and God-consciousness but adds no specific relation to the focus's speech-path pairing.

Explicitly describes the Messenger's call as directed to a straight path.
Contrasts darkness and rejection with being placed upon a straight path.

Confession of sin and condemnation add no new speech-quality or guidance relation.

Directly locates the Messenger upon a straight path, though it adds little beyond fuller route statements.

Links clear signs with God's guidance to a straight path.
Identifies the Quran as guiding to what is most upright and promising righteous believers.
Presents revelation and prophets as means by which believers are guided through human disagreement.
Makes peace a word from the Merciful Lord, a positive divine-speech parallel.
Has the Garden's people praise God for having guided them, joining arrival, guidance, and praise.
Shows people expelled for saying that their Lord is God, a local witness to costly confession.

Links Moses's guidance with a Book inherited by Israel, extending guidance through scripture.

Treats a gracious word and forgiveness as better than charity followed by injury.
Requires an effective word addressed to the inner selves of those acting hypocritically.
Explicitly identifies a straight path of the Lord after signs have been detailed.
Commands following God's straight path and avoiding divergent ways.
Contrasts one who guides to truth with one unable to guide, sharpening divine direction.
Calls to God upon clear insight and names that summons a divinely directed way.
Makes a good word the image of a good tree, directly developing the focus's tayyib speech.
Links the firm word with divine steadiness in this life and the next.
Places the direction of the path with God and distinguishes paths that deviate.
Joins calling to God's way with wisdom, good instruction, and the best manner of discourse.
Commands honorable speech to parents, a concrete instance of ethically good utterance.
Requires an easy and gracious word when material help cannot be given.
Commands believers to say what is best, directly specifying the quality of speech.
Commands gentle speech even when addressing Pharaoh, a salient contrast in speech ethics.
Uses divine light as the enabling image for guidance, complementing the focus's directed path.
Describes the servants of the Merciful answering ignorance with words of peace.
Commands speaking with the People of the Book in the best manner.
Promises those who strive for God that they will be guided to His ways.
Commands God-conscious believers to speak a straight word.
Marks those who turn from false worship and return to God as recipients of good news.
Identifies those who listen to speech and follow its best as the ones God has guided.
Offers to guide the people to the way of right conduct.
Presents calling to God, righteous action, and Muslim identity as the best speech.
Commands repelling evil with what is better, extending the focus's good-speech ethic into response.
Commands holding fast to revelation and explicitly places the Messenger on a straight path.
Defines worship of God as a straight path.
Places the Messenger upon a revealed way in the matter and commands following it.
Describes the Quran as guiding to truth and to a straight path.
States that God increases the guidance of those already guided and grants them reverent awareness.
Describes the Garden as free of vain or sinful speech.
Makes the remaining utterance in the Garden a greeting of peace.
Positively identifies the Quran as the word delivered by a noble messenger.
